coverage.design_evaluation_explanation: Three of six ground-truth variable categories are substantively matched: TorchOpt versus PyTorch gradient methods, computation time, and numerical stability through gradient-reference comparisons and loss measurements.
coverage.design_error_analysis: The design fixes the platform to CPU instead of varying CPU, GPU, and distributed multi-GPU, and replaces ResNet18/ResNet50 with ridge regression and an MLP. Although data and initialization are paired, it uses SGD by default rather than the required fixed Adam configuration and does not clearly fix batch size. Timing measures complete inner solves rather than separate forward/backward durations; stability emphasizes hypergradient error rather than loss evolution and gradient norms.
coverage.conclusion_evaluation_explanation: The conclusion output is empty, so it does not semantically match the ground-truth conclusion.
coverage.conclusion_error_analysis: No conclusion states the expected reduced computation and enhanced numerical stability of TorchOpt or their verification through computation-time and memory-use comparisons with traditional back-propagation.
